## The ATK reference: one-pot penne

The obvious ATK match is **[Instant Pot Parmesan Penne with Chicken and Asparagus](https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/15014-instant-pot-parmesan-penne-with-chicken-and-asparagus)**:

That is genuinely easy by ATK standards: few ingredients, fast HP time, no natural-release wait.

**But** it fights your established workflow in two ways:

1. **Burn risk is higher than adobo.** Starch settles on the bottom. ATK is obsessive about scraping fond and liquid ratios for IP pasta. Your adobo rule — brown outside the pot — does not really apply here; the whole point is one-pot pasta.
2. **Voice lane.** Sweet Filipino spaghetti with hot dogs and banana ketchup would sound like *you*. ATK penne with asparagus sounds like a test kitchen, not Friday-night JoRap.

### B. ATK-style one-pot penne — better ATK fit, weaker JoRap fit

## Best match for JoRap: Filipino spaghetti (ground beef)

This is the obvious one if you want ground beef + pasta in *your* voice:

- **Ground beef** (often with sliced **hot dogs**)
- Sweet tomato base — **banana ketchup**, Filipino-style spaghetti sauce (UFC, Del Monte, etc.), sometimes a little sugar or condensed milk
- Party/kid-birthday energy, not Italian-American marinara

**Instant Pot angle:** Same one-pot skeleton as every other IP spaghetti recipe:

1. Sauté beef (+ onion/garlic) — in the pot or a separate pan if you’re paranoid about fond
2. Add sauce + measured water/broth
3. Layer broken spaghetti on top — **do not stir**
4. Short HP (usually **6–10 min**), quick release, stir at the end

**Why it’s easier to *write* than adobo:** No vinegar-timing rule, no 2 kg batch browning in two skillet loads. Ground beef breaks up fast.

**Why it’s still hard to *publish*:** Liquid ratio is untested in your 8-quart. Too little = burn notice; too much = soup. Your style guide says don’t invent ratios — you need one real cook with a scale.

---

## ATK ground-beef pasta (external)

ATK doesn’t have a flagship **“Instant Pot spaghetti with ground beef”** the way the blogosphere does. Closest references:

| Recipe | Meat | IP? | Notes |
|--------|------|-----|-------|
| [Instant Pot Spaghetti and Turkey Meatballs](https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/15013-instant-pot-spaghetti-and-turkey-meatballs) | Turkey (not beef) | Yes | **Best structural template** — bloom tomato paste/garlic, broth + water, layer pasta, pressure, rest 5–8 min |
| [Pressure-Cooker Easy Ziti with Sausage and Peppers](https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/7536-pressure-cooker-easy-ziti-with-sausage-and-peppers) | Italian sausage | Yes | ATK’s key lesson: **use ziti/penne, not spaghetti strands** — strands clump under pressure |
| [One-Pot Weeknight Pasta Bolognese](https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/16021-one-pot-weeknight-pasta-bolognese) | **1 lb ground beef** | No (Dutch oven) | Great beef technique (baking soda + water for tenderness) but stovetop, not IP |
| [Goan Keema Pasta](https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/17539-goan-keema-pasta) | **1 lb ground beef** | No | Boil pasta separately; brown beef for sauce — not one-pot IP |

So for **ground beef + IP**, you’d borrow ATK’s **turkey meatball spaghetti method** or the **ziti pressure-cooker flow**, and swap in browned ground beef instead of meatballs/sausage.

## Generic IP spaghetti with ground beef (what most people cook)

The internet-converged method (Kitchn, etc.) — useful as a testing baseline, not as publish-ready JoRap numbers:

- **~450 g (1 lb) ground beef**, browned with onion/garlic
- **~680 g (24 oz) jar sauce** + **~480 ml (2 cups) water** (rinse the jar)
- **~225–450 g (8–16 oz) spaghetti**, broken in half, layered, not stirred
- **6–8 min** high pressure, quick release, stir and serve

ATK would push you toward **penne or ziti** instead of spaghetti for even cooking. For Filipino spaghetti, strands are traditional — you’d be choosing nostalgia vs. ATK physics.
